tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet while at MSP gate—land already armed for transit.
Set watches/phones to JST mid-flight and take melatonin at 13:00 CT to align your clock for Dec 16.

2026-12-15.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are dry but near freezing; pack a windproof layer for the Kabukicho neon walk.
tips: Hit the Tokyo Metropolitan Gov't Building 45F deck (free, open till 22:00) for a night Fuji silhouette before konbini nightcap.
Jet-lag crash protocol: anyone hitting the wall hands their konbini order to a squadmate and sleeps without shame.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the outdoor Shibuya Blue Cave illumination walk (~600k LEDs toward Yoyogi).

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shibuya Blue Cave illumination — ~600k blue LEDs toward Yoyogi
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records (9 floors) absorb a full wet afternoon without surfacing.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Blue Cave illumination is an outdoor walk highly vulnerable to December rain; Miyashita Park offers covered, indoor-heavy alternatives.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast—book the exact time online now if not already locked.
If day one cooked the crew, swap Blue Cave for an early nomihodai and 23:00 lights-out.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Nakamise snack gauntlet and Hoppy Street (outdoor market/alley).

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Tokyo National Museum (samurai swords + armor, 2h) slots between Asakusa and Akiba on the same line.
suggestedSwap.reason: Hoppy Street is entirely outdoors and miserable in cold December rain; the Tokyo National Museum is a world-class indoor alternative on the same transit line.

tips: Arrive at Senso-ji by 08:30 to beat the crowds—by 09:30 the main hall is packed.
If Skytree queue is insane, Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door offers the same river view for the price of a beer.

2026-12-18.crowdAlert: teamLab Planets is extremely popular; even with booked tickets, arrive 15 mins early to avoid entry queues.
tips: Hit Tsukiji Outer Market right at 08:00 for the freshest sushi breakfast before the tour groups arrive.
Golden Gai bars seat 5-6 people max; split into smaller groups and rendezvous at a larger bar later.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High rain risk for the coastal Enoden tram views and the Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset. December coastal weather is notoriously fickle.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Hokokuji bamboo temple: Kamakura's quiet bamboo grove with a matcha counter inside it ($4 (¥600)) — an Arashiyama preview minus the crowds.
suggestedSwap.reason: Enoshima island climb offers no cover and poor visibility in rain; Hokokuji provides a covered, atmospheric indoor-outdoor alternative.

tips: If the coastal forecast looks grim by morning, pivot to the FUJI MAXIMALIST swap: ride the Fuji Excursion train to Kawaguchiko for peak December clarity.
Grab a seat on the RIGHT side of the JR south to Kamakura for occasional ocean glimpses.

2026-12-20.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Inokashira Park morning walk and Shimokitazawa vintage maze (mostly outdoor browsing).

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shimokitazawa — vintage maze + curry density record
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: swap Shimokita for Ikebukuro Sunshine City — 3,000-machine gachapon hall + Pokémon Center MEGA under one roof.
suggestedSwap.reason: Shimokitazawa vintage crawling is primarily outdoors; Sunshine City offers massive indoor vintage/otaku alternatives.

tips: Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
Pack FIRST before the Golden Gai encore—bags must close tonight for the morning shinkansen.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Gion at golden hour and Kamo River bank konbini cans.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Gion at golden hour — Hanamikoji + Shirakawa canal
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Kyoto International Manga Museum — 50,000 manga, huge English wall, a school where you just sit and read. Dangerous time vortex.
suggestedSwap.reason: Gion's outdoor charm diminishes in heavy rain; the Manga Museum is an iconic indoor Kyoto alternative.

tips: Grab ekiben at Tokyo Station's Matsuri (200+ kinds) before boarding the Nozomi—Fuji window is at minute 40 on the LEFT.
Send two scouts to L'Escamoteur steampunk bar at 19:40 to hold the queue between dinner and the alley crawl.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Fushimi Inari at dawn and Kiyomizu-dera wooden stage.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kiyomizu-dera — the wooden stage over the valley
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Rain plan: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall. Indoor, jaw-dropping, criminally underrated.
suggestedSwap.reason: Kiyomizu-dera's wooden stage offers no cover and poor views in the rain; Sanjusangendo is a fully indoor, breathtaking alternative.

tips: Vending machine hot corn soup on the Fushimi Inari descent is a December lifesaver.
For the sake curious: hit Sake Bar Yoramu (8 seats) and say 'osusume de'—surrender to the bartender's choice.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses and Nara Park deer diplomacy.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: SNOW PROTOCOL (overrides everything): Kyoto wakes up white → Kinkaku-ji at opening (gold + snow = Japan's rarest photo), Fushimi round two after.
suggestedSwap.reason: If it snows (a rare but real December possibility), the bamboo grove is slippery and dark; Kinkaku-ji in snow is Japan's rarest photo op.

2026-12-23.crowdAlert: Wakakusa-yama mountain climb is closed for the season as of Dec 13—do NOT attempt the hike today.
tips: Bow first to the Nara deer, show empty hands when done—they understand, never run.
Hit Nakatanidou in Naramachi to watch the flying-hammer mochi men in action.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC Christmas buckets sell out fast on Dec 24; pre-order or arrive early to secure the sacred tradition.
tips: If all 8 lost the Nintendo Museum lottery, Uji still carries the morning—Byodo-in, Tsuen tea, and matcha soba are excellent alternatives.
Buy Rikuro's jiggly cheesecake near Namba station ($6/¥965) for the midnight Christmas cake floor party—buy two, they won't survive the night.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ will be at peak Christmas capacity; Express Passes are essential, and Mario Kart single-rider lines cut 60% off wait times.
tips: Rope-drop 45 min early and head straight to SUPER NINTENDO WORLD—timed entry fills up instantly.
If Kinopio's Café is full, Yoshi snack stand + popcorn buckets + Power-Up Band challenges still deliver the serotonin.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Miyajima island and the floating torii; high winds can also cancel ferries.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: ITSUKUSHIMA SHRINE — the torii floating in the sea
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Energy honesty: longest day of the trip. Anyone redlining skips Miyajima, does the museum unhurried, meets us at Hiroshima station.
suggestedSwap.reason: If rain or high winds impact the ferry schedule, spending unhurried time at the Peace Museum is a more reliable and impactful alternative than a rushed, wet island sprint.

tips: Shukkei-en garden is a quiet 10-min walk from the station if the Peace Museum hits heavy—that's the point.
Okonomiyaki schism: Nagata-ya by the Dome is the locals' counter-pick to Okonomimura. Split, eat, debate on the ferry.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the 4km Midosuji Illumination outdoor walk.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: MIDOSUJI ILLUMINATION — 4km of lit boulevard, walked south
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Osaka Museum of Housing & Living: walk a life-size Edo street in a rented yukata — sleeper-hit rain plan, 15 min north.
suggestedSwap.reason: Walking 4km in cold December rain is miserable; the Osaka Museum of Housing & Living is a unique, fully indoor cultural alternative.

tips: Buy 551 Horai butaman 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner—they sell out nightly and house breakfast depends on it.
If Ura-Namba was Wednesday's love story, the JR Tenma standing-bar belt is tonight's sequel—izakaya density world record.

2026-12-28.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Kitano Ijinkan district hill walk and Kobe Harborland at dusk.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kitano Ijinkan district — 19th-century merchant mansions on the hill
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Nada sake district audible: Hakutsuru brewery museum (free, tastings) is two stops from Sannomiya — the Gekkeikan rematch.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Ijinkan district is an exposed hillside walk unpleasant in rain; the Hakutsuru brewery museum is indoor, free, and offers tastings.

tips: Kobe beef budget fork: $22 (¥3,500) Kobe-beef bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Tax-free paperwork check tonight: receipts with passports, purchases accessible—customs CAN ask on exit. 10 minutes now beats a Dec 29 panic.
Sit on the LEFT (seats A) on the Nozomi east for Fuji's encore.
Zero-out your Suica cards and do final boss gachapon at the gate—Japanese whisky allocations beat US prices badly if you buy AFTER security.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.68, your dollar stretches far—withdraw cash at 7-Eleven ATMs for the best rates rather than exchanging at airports, and use Suica for transit and small purchases to minimize fees.

December in Japan is cold and dry with occasional rain; pack versatile layers, a solid windproof/waterproof outer shell, and comfortable walking shoes, as you will average 15-20k steps per day on outdoor temple and market routes.
For a group of 8, always split into two squads of 4 for restaurants, bars, and peak-hour transit—most traditional izakayas and Golden Gai bars physically cannot seat 8 people together.
